Hi Tom / Medisys compliance team —

Thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the security gating items you flagged:

1) SOC 2 status: We confirmed Redwood completed a SOC 2 Type II audit in 2025. I've attached the cover page and our SOC 2 report stub for your review; we can provision the full report under an NDA if you need the auditor workpapers.

2) Data residency & EU region: Redwood has an EU-hosted cluster in Frankfurt that can be pinned for your account. I'll include the data residency matrix as an attachment and note the default behaviour for backups and logs.

3) Cross-border transfers & export controls: You asked about OFAC/ITAR screening for exported models/output. We do not process ITAR-controlled data in our hosted EU region by default; if you have ITAR workloads we recommend our Private deployment option. For OFAC screening, we run entity checks on account provisioning and can add customer-level restrictions.

4) Vendor security questionnaire: Please see the attached XLSX (Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_Medisys.xlsx). Ben will own the initial pass from our side and Karthik will address technical/network items.

Proposed next steps:
- Ben to send completed questionnaire and SOC 2 stub by EOD tomorrow (Nov 3).
- Medisys compliance to confirm whether you need the full SOC 2 report under NDA and share any specific HIPAA/GDPR clauses to call out.
- Jasmine to open HubSpot record (HS-78921) and share DocuSign link for DPA if required.

If anything above is incorrect or missing, flag and I'll update.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Tom — thanks for the questions. Short answers below, and I've attached the initial completed questionnaire for the items we could answer immediately.

1) SOC 2: We can provide the full SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. Sending Docusign to initiate NDA + DPA now: https://www.docusign.com/en/sign/EXAMPLE-dpa
2) Data residency for EU: Yes — backups and logs can be configured to remain in the EU region for dedicated EU accounts. For hosted accounts we offer account-scoped residency with a regional pin; logs can be retained in-region for customers requesting it (we do require a private link for audit log exports). See Redwood_Data_Residency_Map.xlsx for specifics.
3) OFAC/ITAR: To be precise — Redwood does not *intentionally* export ITAR-controlled technical data from the EU region in hosted mode. However, certain model artifacts (trained model weights) can be considered a special-case export; for true ITAR workloads we recommend Redwood Private or a dedicated on-prem deployment. We'll loop legal if you need a formal opinion.

Attached: Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_Medisys_completed_draft.xlsx (partial answers).

I will be available for a short call with Claire and your security engineer tomorrow afternoon if you'd like to walk through the answers.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Claire — thanks, good asks. Attached are two short items: 1) "Model artifact exports — one-pager" (text stub) that clarifies what we treat as an artifact and when it could be considered an export, and 2) a retention table showing audit log retention options for EU-pinned accounts.

Quick bullets:
- Audit logs: configurable retention at account level (30 / 90 / 365 days); PII elements can be redacted at ingestion or truncated on export — we support retention policies to meet GDPR data minimization requests.
- Model artifacts: we consider trained weights, fine-tuned checkpoints, and certain attention-layer cache dumps to be artifacts. Real-time inference outputs (text responses) are not exported as model code; we classify them as customer data. For ITAR concerns where the artifact itself is in scope, we recommend Private deployment; we can provide legal language for procurement.

Ben will follow up with the DocuSign NDA link and a calendar invite for Thu 17:00 CET. I'll also attach the SOC 2 stub again and the residency matrix for Claire's review.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
